title: Snowflake motif — intricate
subtitle: Six branching arms with picot points, 12 cm across in 4-ply cotton
excerpt: The intricate snowflake extends each arm with three branch points and a picot tip, giving a 12 cm snowflake with the crystalline branching of a real ice crystal. Worked in 4-ply cotton on a 2.5 mm hook, it is the display-quality snowflake for framed decorations, wedding table scatter, and gift embellishment.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 6 (1891), intricate lace snowflake chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet star and snowflake chapter.
heroPrompt: An intricate crochet snowflake in white 4-ply cotton with branching picot arms, 12 cm across, on a deep blue velvet background in soft daylight. Six branching arms with picot tips, perfectly symmetrical.

chartDefinition.title: Snowflake motif — intricate
chartDefinition.caption: Magic ring of 12dc. Six main arms, each with two side branches and a picot tip. Main arm: ch-12 out. Branches: ch-5 off the main arm. Picot tip: ch-3 sl-st back.

glossaryTerms.definition: Three chains closed back into the first chain with a slip stitch, forming a small decorative loop. Used at the tips of each arm and branch in this snowflake.

content.text: The intricate snowflake builds each arm in three stages: a main chain length outward, two branch loops at set intervals along the arm, and a
picot

tip at the arm end. The branch loops are simple chain arcs attached to the arm with a slip stitch, mimicking the crystallographic structure of real ice. The final snowflake at 12 cm has 36 points (six arms each with two branches and one tip = three points per arm, but each branch also has a picot giving four points per arm).

Work the main arm chain outward, pausing at two points to add the branch loops, then complete the arm to the picot tip and slip stitch back to the ring. The branch loops are worked hanging off the main arm chain while working outward, before the arm is completed inward.

attrs.title: Materials for one snowflake
attrs.body: About 5 g of white 4-ply cotton. A 2.5 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors. Blocking mat, T-pins, and fabric starch for the finished piece.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished intricate snowflake measures 12 cm across in 4-ply cotton with a 2.5 mm hook, after pinning flat to dry.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), magic ring (MR) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
picot (p) — ch 3, sl st into first ch. Decorative loop.
Pattern
Centre ring
Form a magic ring. Ch 1. Work 12dc into the ring. Sl st to first dc. (12 dc.)
Arms — 6 times

Work 6 arms, attaching each to alternate dc of the ring: *Ch 4. [Side branch: Ch 4. Picot (ch 3, sl st in first ch). Sl st back to the 4th ch of the arm.] Ch 4 more. [Second side branch: Ch 4. Picot. Sl st back to the chain.] Ch 4 more. Picot at arm tip. Sl st back along the remaining chain length to the ring dc. Sl st into next dc of the ring (skip 1dc, then sl st into the next dc for the next arm's start).* Repeat from * to * five more times. Fasten off.

definition.title: Snowflake motif — intricate
definition.caption: 12dc magic ring. Each of six arms: main chain outward with two branch picot loops off the arm chain, picot at arm tip, slip stitch return.

content.text: Finishing

Weave in ends. Dip in fabric starch solution, pin flat to a blocking mat with T-pins at each arm tip and branch tip, and leave to dry fully before removing. The starch sets the snowflake rigid enough to hang or display.
Care
Handwash gently in cool water. Re-starch and re-pin flat to dry if the snowflake has lost rigidity.
What to try next

The joined snowflake (crochet-snowflake-joined) links six basic snowflakes at the arm tips to form a circular wreath. The basic snowflake (crochet-snowflake-basic) is the starting point for anyone new to this construction.
